Problem: Need scalable, reliable hosting for users worldwide.
Solution: Deploy on cloud with auto-scaling, load balancers, CDN.
Implementation: Use Terraform/Pulumi for IaC; Kubernetes or ECS/Fargate.

Problem: Consistent development and deployment environments.
Solution: Package backend services and frontend as Docker containers.
Implementation: Dockerfiles for each service; docker-compose for local dev.

Problem: Automate testing and deployment; reduce human error.
Solution: GitHub Actions/GitLab CI: run tests, build images, deploy.
Implementation: YAML pipelines; integration with cloud registry (ECR/GAR).

Problem: Prevent data loss; comply with data protection regulations.
Solution: Automated daily backups; point-in-time recovery; off-site replication.
Implementation: Managed DB service (RDS, Cloud SQL) backups; cron jobs for file backups.

Problem: Detect issues, performance bottlenecks, errors.
Solution: Collect metrics and logs; set alerts (CPU, memory, error rates).
Implementation: Prometheus + Grafana for metrics; Loki or ELK for logs.

Problem: Prevent abuse of APIs (e.g., AI endpoints).
Solution: Implement rate limiting per user/IP; use WAF (Cloudflare/AWS WAF).
Implementation: Middleware in API gateway (e.g., Redis-based rate limiter).

Problem: Reduce DB load, speed up frequent queries (e.g., syllabus graph).
Solution: Cache proficiency scores, resource lists, user sessions.
Implementation: Redis cluster; cache invalidation on updates.

Problem: Handle async tasks: document parsing, email sending, data exports.
Solution: Queue tasks (e.g., process_pdf.delay()) with workers.
Implementation: Celery (Python) or Bull (Node.js) with Redis as broker.

Problem: Catch and debug production errors quickly.
Solution: Integrate error monitoring SDK into backend and frontend.
Implementation: Sentry SDK; configure source maps for frontend.

Problem: Gradually roll out features; A/B testing.
Solution: Use flag service (LaunchDarkly, Flagsmith, or custom DB).
Implementation: Middleware to check flags; UI conditionals.

Problem: Support multiple client versions without breaking changes.
Solution: Prefix APIs: /api/v1/..., /api/v2/....

Problem: Students, teachers need accounts.
Solution: Email/password; optional social login (Google, Microsoft).
Requirements: Auth library (Auth0, Firebase, or custom Django/Flask).

Problem: Different permissions for student, teacher, admin, school admin.
Solution: Assign roles; middleware checks permissions.
Implementation: Database: users table with role enum; permission matrix in code.

Problem: Prevent fake accounts, ensure email ownership.
Solution: Send verification link on signup; require click before access.

Problem: Users forget passwords.
Solution: “Forgot password” flow with reset token.
Implementation: Similar to verification: email with reset link.

Problem: Enhance security for teacher/admin accounts.
Solution: Option to enable TOTP (Google Authenticator) or SMS.

Problem: Users can request data removal; legal requirement.
Solution: Provide “Delete my account” + confirm; also data export.
Implementation: Soft delete (anonymize) or hard delete after grace period.

Problem: Users can see active sessions and log out remotely.
Solution: Store session tokens in DB; endpoint to revoke.
Implementation: JWT with blacklist or server-side sessions.

Problem: Users view/edit their info, change password, set preferences.
Solution: Profile form: name, school, subjects, target grades.

Problem: Need structured knowledge graph from Edexcel/Cambridge PDFs.
Solution: Extract topics, sub-topics, learning objectives into DB.
Implementation: Python: PyPDF2, regex; store as nodes in Neo4j.

Problem: Students need easy access to past papers + mark schemes.
Solution: Upload PDFs; filter by board, subject, year, variant.

Feature Name: PDF Viewer with Mark Scheme Toggle
Problem: View question paper and mark scheme side-by-side.
Solution: Embed PDF.js with a button to switch/highlight mark scheme.
Implementation: React PDF viewer component; pre-process mark scheme PDFs.

Problem: Provide syllabus-aligned notes.
Solution: Upload HTML/Markdown notes; display with LaTeX support (KaTeX).
Implementation: CMS-like interface; store notes in DB with topic tags.

Problem: Help students grasp abstract concepts via manipulation.
Solution: Embed D3/Three.js simulations (circuit builder, graph transformer, etc.).
Implementation: Custom React components with parameter props; tag to KG nodes.

Problem: Provide distraction-free, syllabus-aligned video content.
Solution: Use YouTube Data API; allow search/filter by approved channels.
Implementation: Backend proxy to YouTube API; store video metadata; restrict channels.
Requirements: YouTube API key; curated channel list.

Problem: Know what students watch; feed into KG.
Solution: Log start, progress, completion; update proficiency for related topics.
Implementation: Event logging via API; batch updates to KG.
Requirements: Video metadata tagged with KG nodes.

Problem: Aid active recall and spaced repetition.
Solution: Generate from notes; user can flip, mark “know” / “still learning”.
Implementation: Simple component; store progress in DB.

Problem: Need searchable, tagged questions for test generation.
Solution: Store each question with metadata (topic, difficulty, marks, type).
Implementation: PostgreSQL table questions with JSON fields for tags.

Problem: Provide instant access to mark schemes for self-assessment.
Solution: Store mark scheme text (with LaTeX) linked to question.
Implementation: Same database row or separate table.

Problem: Teachers want to add their own notes, questions.
Solution: CSV/Excel upload of questions; drag-and-drop for PDFs.
Implementation: Backend parser; validation; frontend upload component.

Problem: Syllabus changes every few years; need to archive old.
Solution: Store valid_from and valid_to dates on topics and questions.
Implementation: Database fields; UI filters to show “2025 syllabus” vs “2028 syllabus”.

Problem: Represent relationships (prerequisites, part-of, related).
Solution: Nodes: Topic, Subtopic; Edges: REQUIRES, PART_OF, RELATED.
Implementation: Ingest parsed syllabus into Neo4j using Cypher queries.

Problem: Track each student’s mastery of each node.
Solution: Store proficiency scores as properties on (Student)-[:MASTERS]->(Topic).
Implementation: Update via attempt logging; store in Neo4j or PostgreSQL with link to Neo4j.

Problem: Retrieve student’s personalized graph for UI.
Solution: API endpoint: /api/kg/{student_id} returns nodes with colors.
Implementation: Cypher query; return JSON for frontend visualization.

Problem: Teacher sees overview of class strengths/weaknesses.
Solution: Aggregate proficiency scores across all students in a class.
Implementation: Database aggregation query (e.g., average per node).

Problem: Students explore topics interactively.
Solution: Use Three.js / D3.js to render nodes, color by proficiency.
Implementation: React component with WebGL; handle node clicks.

Problem: When student struggles, recommend foundational topics.
Solution: Traverse prerequisites edges; check student proficiency; offer review.

Problem: Find specific node by name.
Solution: Search bar; auto-suggest nodes; click to focus graph.
Implementation: Frontend filtering of graph data; backend search API.

Problem: Store embeddings of past papers, mark schemes, notes.
Solution: Chunk documents, generate embeddings (OpenAI or local).

Problem: Answer student questions based on authoritative sources.
Solution: Retrieve relevant chunks; feed to LLM with prompt.
Implementation: Hybrid search (vector + keyword); LLM (GPT-4, Claude, or local).

Problem: Students interact with tutor.
Solution: Chat window with message history, citations, source links.

Problem: Maintain context across multiple turns.
Solution: Store chat history in DB; inject recent messages into LLM context.

Problem: Show source (past paper, mark scheme) for each claim.
Solution: Return source IDs with answer; frontend shows link to PDF.
Implementation: Retrieve source metadata from vector DB.

Problem: Help students continue learning.
Solution: Generate 3 recommended questions based on current conversation.
Implementation: LLM prompt or rule-based from KG.

Problem: Students can upload photos of handwritten work or diagrams.
Solution: Use vision LLM (GPT-4V, Claude 3) to process image.
Implementation: Extend API to accept multipart form; vision model integration.

Problem: Accessibility; faster input.
Solution: Use browser Web Speech API or backend STT (Whisper).

Problem: Students need instant, exam-specific feedback on answers.
Solution: Compare student answer to mark scheme using LLM; return marks + feedback.
Implementation: Prompt engineering; score extraction; store attempt.

Problem: Students often write on paper; upload photo.
Solution: Use OCR + LLM to extract text; then Smart Mark.
Implementation: Tesseract or cloud OCR; image preprocessing.

Problem: Students want custom practice on weak topics.
Solution: Generate quiz from question bank filtered by KG weak nodes, difficulty, length.
Implementation: Query builder; select random questions; compile PDF + interactive UI.

Problem: Teachers create custom tests quickly.
Solution: UI for teachers to select topics/difficulty; generate print-friendly PDF.
Implementation: Similar to Target Test but teacher-facing; plus answer key.

Problem: Simulate real exam structure (topic weighting, question types).
Solution: Analyze past papers to create blueprint (e.g., “Mechanics 35%”); then generate.

Problem: Create urgency, simulate real exam window.
Solution: Offer unseen mock papers for 2 weeks; after deadline, provide predicted grade.
Implementation: Event table; grade boundaries; email notifications.

Problem: Practice time management.
Solution: Countdown timer; auto-submit; log time per question.

Problem: Students forget flagged questions.
Solution: Schedule reviews at optimal intervals (1,3,7,14,30 days).
Implementation: Background job; store next_review date on attempts.

Problem: Students lose track of what they’ve solved.
Solution: Log each attempt: score, time, confidence, flag.

Problem: Note which questions are difficult, include doubt type.
Solution: UI: flag icon, doubt type selector; store in attempt table.

Problem: Mark when problem is understood.
Solution: “Resolved” button clears flag; adds proficiency bonus.

Problem: Avoid repeating same question unintentionally.
Solution: Display badge “Attempted on [date]” when viewing question.
Implementation: Check attempt table; small UI component.

Problem: Central place to see problematic questions, due reviews, weak topics.
Solution: Tabbed interface showing lists from attempts and KG.

Problem: Students need overview of progress, recommendations, recent activity.
Solution: Cards: KG summary, due reviews, next steps, predicted grade.

Problem: See improvement over time, topic mastery.
Solution: Line charts (performance trend), bar charts (topic proficiency).
Implementation: Chart.js / Recharts; data from analytics endpoints.

Problem: Plan revision schedule based on exam date and KG.
Solution: AI suggests daily/weekly topics; user can drag events.
Implementation: React Big Calendar; backend scheduling algorithm.

Problem: Know current standing relative to target.
Solution: Use proficiency and past performance to estimate grade (A*–U).
Implementation: Regression model using historical grade boundaries.

Problem: Encourage daily usage.
Solution: Track consecutive days with activity; display badge.

Problem: Reward milestones (10 mastered topics, 30-day streak).
Solution: Define badge rules; award when triggers met; show in profile.

Problem: Keep students informed about reminders, events.
Solution: In-app bell icon with list of notifications; optional email.
Implementation: Notifications table; background job to create.

Problem: Help students focus.
Solution: Embedded timer; log study sessions.

Problem: Manage student groups.
Solution: CRUD classes; add/remove students by email or CSV upload.

Problem: See all students in class.
Solution: List students; links to individual student dashboards.

Problem: Assign resources (notes, quizzes, past papers) to class/individual.
Solution: Teacher selects resource, due date; students see on dashboard.

Problem: Grade and give feedback on student work.
Solution: List submissions; inline grading (for subjective questions).
Implementation: Similar to submission inbox; integration with Smart Mark.

Problem: See which topics the whole class struggles with.
Solution: Aggregate student KGs; color-coded nodes.
Implementation: Backend aggregation; frontend same graph component.

Problem: Identify students falling behind.
Solution: Compute risk score based on engagement, proficiency drop, unresolved flags.

Problem: Quick overview of classes, recent assignments, flagged students.
Solution: Cards: alerts, pending grading, class average.

Problem: Send messages to class.
Solution: Create announcement; students see in-app and optionally email.

Problem: Teachers can add custom questions not visible to students.
Solution: Separate flag teacher_only on questions; hidden from student queries.

Problem: Download grades for offline analysis.
Solution: Export assignment scores, predicted grades.

Problem: See class-level improvement over time.
Solution: Line charts of average scores; bar charts of question difficulty.

Problem: Generate lesson plans, worksheets, model answers.
Solution: Teacher asks natural language; AI uses KG+resources.

Problem: Monitor platform health, user counts, revenue.
Solution: Metrics cards, graphs, recent errors.

Problem: View, suspend, delete users; assign roles.
Solution: Admin table with actions.

Problem: Remove inappropriate user-generated content (forum posts).
Solution: Review queue; approve/delete.

Problem: Change settings without deployment.
Solution: Admin panel to toggle features, set rate limits.

Problem: Handle payments for premium plans and school licenses.
Solution: Integrate Stripe; manage plans, invoices, webhooks.

Problem: Understand business performance.
Solution: Charts: DAU, MAU, conversion, churn.

Problem: Customize notification emails.
Solution: Admin editor for email HTML; variables.

Problem: Cold start, no interaction data.
Solution: Recommend syllabus order + popular resources among similar students.
Implementation: Simple association rules: “students who did X did Y”.

Problem: Recommend similar resources to what student engaged with.
Solution: Use question tags; compute similarity via embedding or topic overlap.

Problem: Use patterns across users to predict preferences.
Solution: Train model (e.g., LightFM) on user-resource interactions.

Problem: Combine multiple signals for best results.
Solution: Rule-based → content-based → collaborative based on data sparsity.

Problem: Avoid echo chamber, ensure syllabus coverage.
Solution: With 10% probability, recommend random untouched topic.
Implementation: Random sampling from topics with zero attempts.

Problem: Tell student exactly what to study next based on weak nodes.
Solution: Query KG for weakest node (lowest proficiency) that has prerequisites met.

Problem: Build trust; show why item was recommended.
Solution: Display “Because you struggled with X” or “Because you watched Y”.

Problem: Teachers want insights without SQL.
Solution: Input box: “Show me students who struggle with photosynthesis”.
Implementation: LLM translates to SQL or API calls; return data.

Problem: Identify widespread errors in free-text answers.
Solution: Cluster student responses using embeddings; flag frequent wrong answers.

Problem: Save teacher time preparing progress reports.
Solution: Click “Generate Report” → PDF with class summary, weak topics.
Implementation: Report template (LaTeX/HTML to PDF); backend generation.

Problem: Quick check on individual student.
Solution: Teacher asks: “How is Alex doing in calculus?” → returns proficiency, recent attempts.

Problem: Show which topics need more teaching.
Solution: Aggregate proficiency across class; highlight topics below threshold.

Problem: Students study everywhere.
Solution: Use CSS Grid/Flexbox, media queries; mobile-first design.

Problem: Reduce eye strain; user preference.
Solution: Toggle; system preference detection; CSS variables.

Problem: Support students with disabilities.
Solution: Keyboard navigation, screen reader labels, color contrast, ARIA attributes.

Problem: New users learn features quickly.
Solution: Step-by-step overlay (e.g., Driver.js) on first login.

Problem: Power users navigate faster.
Solution: Common actions: Ctrl+K for search, ? for help.

Problem: Improve perceived performance.
Solution: Show placeholder cards while data loads.

Problem: Provide feedback on actions (submit, save).
Solution: Use toast library (react-hot-toast).

Problem: Accidental deletion of flagged question, etc.
Solution: Snackbar with “Undo” after destructive action.

Problem: Quickly find notes, questions, videos.
Solution: Elasticsearch or PostgreSQL full-text search; auto-suggest.

Problem: Narrow down content.
Solution: Multi-select dropdowns; update results dynamically.

Problem: Let students arrange their dashboard.
Solution: Drag-and-drop layout (e.g., react-grid-layout); save preference.

Problem: Native-like experience without app store.
Solution: Service worker; manifest; offline caching.
Implementation: Workbox; generate with React PWA template.

Problem: Students without internet.
Solution: Allow downloading notes, past papers, flashcards to cache.
Implementation: IndexedDB with local storage; sync when online.

Problem: Push notifications, better performance.
Solution: Build native app wrapper (optional later).

Problem: Encrypt data in transit.
Solution: Use TLS certificates (Let’s Encrypt).
Implementation: Configure load balancer or reverse proxy.

Problem: Handle EU user data.
Solution: Cookie consent, data export, deletion, privacy policy.

Problem: Protect database contents.
Solution: Enable AWS RDS encryption; encrypt backups.

Problem: Track who did what for compliance.
Solution: Log user actions (login, content modify, assignment grade).
Implementation: Middleware to insert into audit table.

Problem: Common web attacks.
Solution: Use CSRF tokens; sanitize user input; CSP headers.

Problem: Prevent brute force, abuse.
Solution: See infrastructure section.

Problem: Enable frontend and third-party integrations.
Solution: Design consistent REST endpoints; OpenAPI spec.

Problem: Easy login for schools.
Solution: Add OAuth providers.

Problem: Embed into Canvas, Moodle as external tool.
Solution: Implement LTI standard; allow deep linking.

Problem: Allow external services to react (e.g., new assignment).
Solution: Register webhook URLs; send POST on events.

Problem: Communicate limits to clients.
Solution: Include X-RateLimit-* headers in responses.

Problem: Students need peer help.
Solution: Topic-based discussion threads; upvote best answers.
Implementation: Basic forum database schema; moderation tools.

Problem: Separate assessment from practice.
Solution: Questions marked teacher_only appear only in teacher-assigned tests.

Problem: Schools want custom branding.
Solution: Allow school admin to upload logo, set primary color.
Implementation: Dynamic CSS variables; store school branding.

Problem: Add many students at once.
Solution: Upload CSV with emails/names; create accounts and enroll.

Problem: GDPR right to data portability.
Solution: Provide JSON/CSV download of all personal data and attempts.

Problem: Keep parents/students informed.
Solution: Weekly digest: completed papers, weak topics, predicted grade.

Problem: Real-time help for platform issues.
Solution: Integrate third-party widget (Intercom, Crisp).
